home.badge: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)
home.headline2: From the poles to the public.
home.intro: A prototype outreach portal for NCPOR's work: four decades of Indian expeditions to Antarctica, the Arctic and the Himalayas, with every report, dataset, photo and video credited to its source.
home.latestSubtitle: Reports, datasets, publications and media from the archive
home.howTitle: One upload becomes an archive record, a news story and a school lesson.
home.step1Body: Expedition reports, publications, datasets, photos and videos go into one archive, with station, expedition and year attached.
home.step2Body: Each item gets a scientific summary, a plain-language summary and a Hindi summary, plus keywords and search indexing. Even scanned reports.
home.step3Body: Nothing goes public until a DHRUV reviewer approves it. The person who drafted a post cannot approve it.
home.step4Body: Website news, social media posts, class-wise lessons with certificates, and answers in Ask Dhruv, in English and Hindi.
home.learnTitle: Lessons built from real expedition reports
home.learnBody: Short science lessons for Class 6 to 12, each with a quiz. Score 80% and download a verifiable certificate.
home.askTitle: Ask a question, get an answer with sources
home.askBody: Answers come only from the archive, and every fact links back to the document it came from.
home.askSample: What happened at Himansh station in winter for the first time?
home.heroCredit: Photo: Thamban Meloth, CC BY-SA 4.0, toned · India's first scientific expedition to the South Pole, 2010
home.heroPhotoAlt: Members of India's first scientific expedition to the South Pole in red polar suits, kneeling and standing behind a banner reading "1st Indian Scientific Expedition to South Pole 2010-2011", with the Indian flag behind them
home.scrollerIntro: India's expeditions to Antarctica, the Arctic and the Himalaya, oldest first. Every date on these cards links to its source.

accuracy.title: How accurate is Ask Dhruv?
accuracy.intro: We test Ask Dhruv with a fixed set of questions in English and Hindi. Each question has an answer we checked against its source. Every result is shown below, failures included.
accuracy.statCorrectHint: Questions the archive can answer: the answer has the checked facts and cites the item they come from.
accuracy.statRefuse: Said "not in the archive" when it should
accuracy.statRefuseHint: Questions the archive cannot answer: Dhruv should say so and not answer from general knowledge.
accuracy.statLangHint: Hindi questions answered in Hindi, English in English.
accuracy.lastRun: Last run {date} · {engine} · typical answer time {secs} s
accuracy.engineOpen: open-source model {model} on our own computer
accuracy.how1: The questions are fixed. We add new ones over time and never change a question to fit an answer.
accuracy.how2: A question passes only if the answer contains every checked fact and cites an archive item that holds it. A right answer without the right source fails.
accuracy.how3: Grading is automatic: it looks for the checked facts in the answer text, in English or Hindi. A person reads every failure.
accuracy.how4: The test runs through the same code as the Ask page, with the same public access.
accuracy.whySource: Right facts, but not the right source
accuracy.whyAnswered: Answered instead of saying it doesn't know
accuracy.whyError: The AI service failed during the run
accuracy.askLink: How accurate is Dhruv? See the test results

verifyPost.unknownLead: No DHRUV post has this code. Check that you typed it correctly, and treat the post with caution.
verifyPost.compare: If the post you saw says something different, it was changed after approval. Trust this version.
